blocks.note: Home of the GranMorgu development (Sapakara South and Krabdagu fields), about 150 km offshore. FID October 2024. First oil targeted 2028.

4,749 km2. Sloanea gas field declared commercial in late 2025; a floating LNG development is the leading concept with FID targeted in the second half of 2026 and first gas around 2030. Roystonea and Fusaea oil finds still under evaluation.

players.r: State oil company and resource manager
players.d: Founded in 1980 and 100% state owned. Staatsolie is both a producer (onshore fields, the Tout Lui Faut refinery, power generation, a gold royalty from Rosebel) and the body that manages Suriname's petroleum acreage: it markets blocks, negotiates production sharing contracts and can take up to a 20% share in any development.
Operator of GranMorgu, Suriname's first offshore development, and a partner or operator across several other blocks.
Formerly Apache. Drilled the original Maka Central discovery in 2020 and holds 40% of Block 58.
Holds the gas story: Sloanea, Roystonea and Fusaea in Block 52, plus positions in Blocks 53, 63, 64 and shallow-offshore acreage.
Entered through the Demerara round and a farm-out from Chevron, targeting deeper plays.
The main shallow-water explorer, working with Paradise Oil Company and QatarEnergy.
A recurring non-operating partner alongside TotalEnergies, Chevron and Shell.
Building the GranMorgu FPSO on a Fast4Ward hull, in partnership with Technip Energies. Together with Suriname they run the STS joint venture and its graduate programme.
Partner to SBM Offshore on the GranMorgu FPSO.
Won the roughly US$1.9 billion subsea scope on GranMorgu.
Supplying subsea production systems, including the Christmas trees assembled and tested in Malaysia.
The vehicle Staatsolie uses to hold working interests in shallow offshore blocks.

timeline.d: The first oil in Suriname is found in Nickerie district, on the coastal plain near the Guyana border. Nothing commercial follows, and systematic exploration only begins in the early 1960s.
A Geological Mining Department crew drilling for drinking water in Saramacca district hits heavy oil in a school yard. That accident is the Tambaredjo field.
The state creates its own oil company on 13 December 1980 rather than leaving the resource to foreign operators.
Commercial production starts at Tambaredjo on 25 November 1982, at 200 barrels a day. Output is small but it funds everything that follows.
Staatsolie starts refining its own crude rather than exporting all of it, initially into asphalt bitumen and fuel oil.
A roughly US$1 billion upgrade lifts the plant to around 15,000 to 16,000 barrels a day and adds diesel and gasoline.
Apache and Total hit oil in Block 58. Kwaskwasi, Sapakara West and PETRONAS's Sloanea gas find follow in the same year.
Appraisal drilling proves the two fields that will become GranMorgu.
TotalEnergies and APA sanction GranMorgu, committing about US$10.5 billion. Staatsolie exercises its 20% back-in right.

Staatsolie raises more than US$2 billion, including a US$516 million bond and a US$1.6 billion syndicated loan from 18 lenders, to fund its US$2.4 billion share. Saipem, SBM Offshore and Technip Energies start work.
Staatsolie opens roughly 60% of offshore acreage, more than 70,000 km2, to nomination by companies at any time instead of waiting for a bid round.

timeline.t: A ministry for oil and gas
timeline.d: The new government creates the Ministry of Oil, Gas and Environment, headed by former Staatsolie manager Patrick Brunings.
The FPSO hull enters dry dock in China, the first subsea equipment lands at the Dr. Jules Sedney Terminal in Paramaribo, and subsea trees roll off the line in Malaysia.
All mineral revenue is supposed to flow into the Savings and Stabilisation Fund. The IMF notes the fund still needs a board, procedures and an investment framework.
Up to 32 producer and injector wells are planned for GranMorgu.
PETRONAS targets an FID on a floating LNG development in Block 52.
The vessel leaves the yard for Suriname; installation and commissioning offshore follow.
GranMorgu is targeted to start producing, ramping toward 220,000 barrels a day. The IMF projects GDP growth around 55% in the first full year.
If Sloanea is sanctioned, Suriname could export LNG for the first time. The IMF sees crude output peaking around 73 million barrels in 2030 and 2031.

glossary.d: 159 litres of oil. Production is quoted in barrels per day (bpd or b/d).
A numbered area of seabed that the state licenses to a company for exploration and production.
Production Sharing Contract. The company pays the costs and takes the risk; the state keeps ownership of the oil and takes a royalty plus a share of the profit oil.
The company that actually runs the work on a block. Other companies in the block are non-operating partners and just pay their share.
Final Investment Decision. The moment partners commit the money and construction can start. GranMorgu reached FID in October 2024.
Floating Production, Storage and Offloading vessel. A ship that receives oil from the seabed, separates it, stores it and offloads it to tankers. GranMorgu uses one instead of a fixed platform.
The valve stack that sits on the seabed on top of a well. Also called a Christmas tree.
Connecting a new field to existing production equipment by pipeline, instead of building a whole new facility. Cheap and fast, which is why nearby discoveries matter.
Floating Liquefied Natural Gas. A vessel that chills gas to liquid at sea so it can be shipped. The leading concept for Sloanea.
Under a PSC the company first recovers its costs from a slice of production (cost oil, 75 to 80% in Suriname), and the rest (profit oil) is split with the state.
Staatsolie's option to take up to 20% of a development once it is proven, by paying its 20% of the costs from that point on.
The share of the work, spend and jobs that goes to Surinamese companies and workers.
The total share of project value the state ends up with through royalty, profit oil, taxes and its Staatsolie stake. Roughly 60 to 70% in Suriname after costs.
